# 長天期美債回升，油價大漲仍壓抑短端

## 曲線趨平，反映兩種不同風險

週五經濟數據強弱互見，科技股再跌，資金轉向較長天期美債；短端卻往反方向走。2年期殖利率上升2個基點至4.18%，10年期下降2個基點至4.55%，30年期下降3個基點至5.06%。曲線因而趨平，反映市場一邊衡量成長敏感項目轉弱，一邊防範油價與持續性價格壓力，最終仍可能迫使聯準會進一步升息。

通膨連結債最清楚呈現了這個分歧。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點至2.31%，損益兩平通膨率卻隨布蘭特原油大漲4.59%至$88.10，上升2個基點至2.24%。實質殖利率降低支撐長債，但當天並不是全面的通膨降溫行情。本週CPI、PPI較溫和後，市場估計7月升息機率只剩約15%，卻仍計入年底前至少升息一次。

信用債投資人的選擇也更細緻。大型雲端業者債券繼續承受全球發行量增加的壓力，Cotality則在改變融資組合、提供大幅價格與契約讓步後，終於完成再融資。Foundever債權人接受減債與股權安排，Aston Martin研議中的融資卻引發既有債權順位疑慮。這不是所有融資都已關閉，而是借款人條件與債權結構，決定了取得資金必須付出的代價。

## 活動數據不一，油價讓聯準會更難放鬆警戒

週五數據沒有重現週四強勁的製造業訊號。6月工業生產僅增加0.1%，製造業持平，礦業與公用事業各增0.4%。產能利用率維持76.1%，比長期平均低3.3個百分點。

新屋開工總額看似強勁，月增19.0%至年率142.7萬戶，但增長主要來自多戶住宅。單戶開工反而減少0.2%至89.5萬戶；建照下降3.0%至136.7萬戶，其中單戶建照下降2.4%至87.1萬戶。完工增加3.3%，單戶完工增加6.6%。施工與成屋供給增加，尚不能證明家庭購屋需求也同步加速。

進口價格則顯示通膨傳導仍有壓力。6月月增0.3%，5月修正為增加1.7%；年增率7.1%，為2022年8月以來最高。燃料進口價格在5月大漲12.6%後回落0.4%，非燃料價格卻月增0.4%、年增4.2%。出口價格則由修正後的月增1.2%轉為下降0.6%。相較先前CPI與PPI帶來的印象，價格改善並沒有那麼全面。

消費者信心初值升至5個月高點，較低汽油價格改善了民眾感受，一年期通膨預期由4.6%降至4.2%。但到週五收盤，燃料環境又已改變：最新一波油價上漲，可能侵蝕這份以先前汽油回落為基礎的改善。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁哈瑪克尤其強調這項風險。相較勞動市場轉弱，她更擔心通膨，並認為就業已接近自己估計的充分就業水準；企業則反映能源、供應鏈、保險與AI需求帶來的價格壓力。這延續了洛根前一天的偏鷹立場，即使本週通膨數據降低了下一次會議立即行動的急迫性。市場關注的逐漸變成持續性壓力何時迫使聯準會回應，而不只是7月是否實現先前擔心的升息。

5年期殖利率維持4.28%。短天期未跟隨長端上漲，使2s10s收窄4個基點至37個基點，2s30s收在88個基點。儘管各項數據公布後波動不小，一週合計變化仍有限：2年期、5年期、10年期分別下降3、2、1個基點，30年期持平；四個天期都仍比一個月前高12至13個基點。

短端以外的實質殖利率普遍下降。5年期與7年期各降3個基點至2.01%、2.15%，20年期與30年期各降4個基點至2.67%、2.87%。10年期實質殖利率下降4個基點，卻有一半被通膨補償增加抵銷，名目殖利率因此只下降2個基點。較短天期短券走強，較長短券殖利率仍偏高，52週券達4.00%。眼前資金壓力不明顯，但對政策敏感的曲線區段仍保留稍後升息的可能。

## 再融資能完成，但條件明顯變貴

Cotality解決了週四收盤時尚未確定的融資問題。初步需求偏弱後，這家房地產資料公司把部分資金來源由債券移向貸款，合計籌得$52.5億。$28億定期貸款以98價格、425個基點利差定價；$16.5億第一順位債以面額發行，殖利率9%；$8億第二順位債以95發行，殖利率約13.3%，為今年美國新發高收益債最高。

投資人也取得更強保障，以防公司透過庭外重整手法改變債權地位。資金用於重整5年前$60億收購留下的債務，但公司評等仍比投資級低6級，負債約為獲利8倍，3月底現金僅約$5,500萬，現在又增加了債息成本。即使眼前發行關卡通過，自由現金流預期極低、仍需依賴循環額度的問題並未消失。

投資級市場的新資訊，則是大型雲端業者債券表現落後的規模與廣度。Alphabet、Meta、Amazon與甲骨文自2025年初以來，已發行超過$3,000億，其中近$800億以英鎊、歐元、日圓等非美元幣別籌措。約79%的債券利差高於上市首日，平均價格比發行價低3.3點，總報酬為−1.4%，在各自發行市場都屬表現最弱的族群之一。

供給累積速度超出許多投資組合預期。當美元市場難以單獨輕易承接全部需求，這些業者便擴大海外發行。Amazon最新$250億交易的超額認購程度，以大型AI融資而言異常偏低。保險資金仍有承接空間，但受指數約束的投資組合，早已隨權重增加而累積曝險。資本計畫繼續推進，意味著AI回報疑慮升高時，市場仍可能面對更多新債，而不是借款自動減少。

軟銀也尋求另一條融資管道，計畫發行約¥600億機構債；此前已透過日本零售次順位債籌措¥6,780億，並在今年稍早發行美元及歐元債。AI承諾包括對OpenAI近$650億投資，原先以該持股擔保、規劃約$100億的貸款，已縮小至約$60億。這家BB+借款人仍能動用零售、機構、海外與擔保融資，但管道如此多元，也反映待支付承諾的龐大規模。

Foundever的協議處理的是已無法照原條件維持的債務。參與債權人預計以每$1舊債換取57.5美分新定期貸款，取得重整後約35%股權，並分享$2.5億現金償還。Mulliez家族將投入$2.25億新股權，其餘由公司提供，債務預估減少約$9億。債權人指導委員會成員另取得10美分回收，使協商中的位置直接影響最終結果。

Aston Martin則討論把資產移到既有債權人追索範圍之外，再以這些資產擔保借款的安排。債權人先前已因順位疑慮結盟，公司英鎊2029年到期債券仍下跌近10便士至61。Howden考慮的方向相反：以大型增資及日後上市改善資產負債表，目標估值£500億，並用所得降低優先債務。歷經5年約250筆收購後，該公司的優先債務已達獲利5.1倍。

規模約$1.3兆的CLO市場，則面對扣除債務融資成本後、留給股權部位的報酬縮水。貸款表現偏弱、軟體業損失，以及併購貸款供給不足，壓縮了資產收入與資金成本之間的利差。這不代表優先順位融資已停擺，卻可能使新增貸款需求更在意價格，並促使管理人考慮現金流不同的基礎設施或設備資產。

發行計畫仍然活躍。德意志銀行正為Baker Tilly準備約$30億債務，以取代與Moss Adams合併相關的私人信貸。聖安東尼奧規劃$9.44億市政債，支應20年期機場擴建，其中新航廈成本約$17億。

公共建設也出現契約保障問題。加拿大支付了戈迪豪大橋全部C$64億建造成本，但新安排讓美國在前15年取得50%營運淨收入，卻未明確先扣除加拿大應付利息與本金。原先架構容許加拿大保留通行費，直到債務清償。這項改變使付款順序、車流及收費政策，更直接影響加拿大能否收回融資成本。

主要信用債基金的波動遠小於部分借款人的處境。LQD上漲0.06%至107.56，HYG下跌0.19%至79.65，JNK下跌0.10%至95.98。這些小幅變化，與再融資完成、債權人大幅讓步、供給負擔增加同時存在，而不是融資管道一致關閉。

## 歐洲通膨降溫，日本正常化仍在視野內

歐元區6月HICP年增率由5月的3.2%降至2.8%，符合初值，月減0.1%。服務業貢獻年增率1.51個百分點，能源0.77個百分點，食品、酒精與菸草0.29個百分點，非能源工業財0.18個百分點。22個歐盟國家通膨下降，廣泛降溫增加了等待的理由，儘管通膨仍高於一年前。

經濟學家預期ECB在7月維持不變，多數認為取得新預測後，9月將升息25個基點，使存款利率達2.5%。官員尚未看到薪資使能源衝擊固化的明顯證據，德國央行總裁納格爾仍維持警戒。燃料供應若再遭干擾，前景可能比歷史性的6月數據更快改變。

日本銀行會議前的報導則指出，官員可能在6月升息後維持1%政策利率，並考慮上修截至明年3月會計年度的0.5%成長預估。即使能源進口昂貴，AI相關出口仍支持利潤與所得；企業成本轉嫁加快、通膨高於目標，也使再升息預期持續。交換市場估計10月以前行動的機率約69%。

日本3個月短券標售加權平均殖利率為0.9618%，最低得標價格對應殖利率0.9695%。競標金額¥11.5723兆，接受¥2.89786兆，另有¥9,021億非競標分配；7月21日發行，10月19日到期。短期工具需求仍正常，但最終政策路徑與較長天期日本公債供給，仍是不同問題。

官員也持續強調規模¥293.6兆的GPIF應投資國內資產，但其日本債、日本股、海外債、海外股各25%的策略配置沒有改變。這些談話與國內需求及弱勢日圓的政策討論有關，卻不代表已出現新買盤。歐洲通膨降溫、日本成長展望增強，仍讓海外存續期間需求受到不同方向牽引。

## 油價曝險與融資選擇，拉開新興市場差異

EMB下跌0.06%至95.53，一週下跌0.48%，一個月下跌1.18%。紐約收盤時美元幾乎持平，油價反而是更重要的分歧來源：出口國可能增加收入，其他國家卻面對更高進口、補貼與通膨成本。

印度尤其敏感。通膨近一年半來首次超過央行目標後，印度央行總裁馬霍特拉形容物價偏高。印度近90%石油依賴進口，歷來其中近一半經過荷莫茲海峽。央行利率維持5.25%，盧比約96.32兌$1，10年期政府債殖利率約6.75%。最新攻擊與偏弱季風，可能讓央行更難忽略進口成本上升。

巴西考慮最快今年首次在中國境內發行約CNY100億、折合$14.8億的熊貓債。官員希望主權指標券能替在中國有重要業務的企業開啟人民幣融資。外匯連結債務僅占巴西總債務4%，該國今年已發行€50億，為最大一筆全球交易，也是逾10年來首次歐元發行。熊貓債增加的是融資市場，而非取代既有美元基礎。

阿根廷產油省份內烏肯，正尋求2017年以來首次國際發債，已取得最高$5億授權，目標是5至7年、到期一次還本，利率7%至8%。頁岩油產出增加支持收入前景，阿根廷利差收窄也讓數個省份得以發行，即使中央政府仍未重返市場。單一到期日與商品收入依賴，仍是這項融資的重要特徵。

智利政府主張，降低公司稅、加快投資許可，可讓2027年成長達3.7%，高於未採行方案的2.7%，並使2029年總債務占GDP為44.2%，而非45.3%。改善前提是成長能抵銷稅收損失。分析師警告，若超過政府45%的審慎債務門檻，可能威脅評等，因此投資與活動究竟會有多大反應，是財政論述的核心。

## 科技股續弱，原油大幅上漲

S&P 500下跌1.01%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.49%，半導體指數下跌1.63%。半導體一週累計下跌9.97%，比一個月前低逾12%；VIX上升12.19%至18.77。撤退焦點仍在科技，而非損失無差別擴散到信用市場。

中國Moonshot推出低成本模型，加深了對競爭及基礎設施支出回報的疑問。當前獲利與需求並未崩壞，但估值對回收期較長的投資已不再那麼寬容。股市轉弱提供債券支持，持續需要支付建設支出，卻又讓大型雲端業者債券承壓。

美國與伊朗攻擊持續，WTI大漲4.48%至$82.49，布蘭特上漲4.59%至$88.10，一週漲幅分別達15.52%、15.91%。這有助於解釋，為什麼長債上漲時通膨補償仍提高，政策敏感天期也未跟進。同樣地，最新油價也威脅了消費者預期中反映的先前汽油利多。

美元指數幾乎持平於100.75，一週小跌。黃金期貨上升0.68%至$4,012.70，但整週仍下跌2.23%。避險需求並不一致：實質殖利率降低幫助黃金收復部分跌幅，能源可能使政策利率長期偏高，卻構成另一股力量。

週一亞洲早盤，攻擊擴大至軍事目標以外，布蘭特一度再漲3.8%、突破$91，美元對多數貨幣走強。日本假日使亞洲時段美債現券交易休市，投資人仍需等待利率市場對進一步能源衝擊的反應；這是週五收盤後的新發展。

## 美國下一輪重點是通膨保障與房市需求

7月23日美東13:00的$210億新10年期TIPS標售，將在油價大漲後測試實質存續期間與通膨保障的需求。6月新屋銷售接著於7月24日10:00公布。標售承接與房市需求，有助於判斷7月28至29日聯準會會議前，週五較低實質殖利率能否與能源帶動的較高通膨補償並存。

7月23日ECB決議、7月24日美東02:00英國零售銷售，提供歐洲觀點。6月通膨降溫、薪資外溢有限，有利央行保持耐心；但能源衝擊若延續，政策措辭與家庭支出將顯示還剩多少等待空間。

日本7月24日全國CPI在央行決議前公布。若成長展望改善、通膨仍廣泛偏高，將支持進一步正常化預期；若價格轉緩，或家庭需求承壓，則支持等待。影響不只在下一次升息，也包括日本公債需求、日圓，以及海外債券對日本投資人的相對吸引力。

overall_summary.headline: 長天期美債回升，油價大漲仍壓抑短端

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Long Treasuries recover, but surging oil keeps the front end under pressure

## A flatter curve reflects two different risks

Long Treasuries rallied on Friday as uneven economic data and another technology selloff drew investors toward duration. The front end moved the other way. The 2-year yield rose 2 basis points to 4.18%, while the 10-year fell 2 to 4.55% and the 30-year declined 3 to 5.06%. The resulting flattening captured a market weighing weaker growth-sensitive signals against the risk that oil and persistent price pressure would eventually require more Fed tightening.

The distinction was clearest in inflation-linked bonds. The 10-year real yield fell 4 basis points to 2.31%, but its breakeven rose 2 to 2.24% as Brent jumped 4.59% to $88.10. Lower real yields supported long bonds without making the session another broad disinflation rally. Traders still saw only about a 15% chance of a July increase after the week's softer CPI and PPI, while retaining at least one increase by year-end.

Credit buyers were making similarly differentiated decisions. Hyperscaler bonds continued to struggle under heavy global supply, and Cotality completed its refinancing only after shifting the financing mix and granting substantial price and covenant concessions. Elsewhere, lenders accepted debt reduction and equity in Foundever, while Aston Martin's prospective financing raised concern over existing creditors' priority. These were not signs that all funding had closed: they showed how much the terms of access depended on the borrower and the claims being offered.

## Mixed activity supports real duration, while oil complicates the Fed outlook

Friday's releases did not repeat Thursday's strong manufacturing message. June industrial production rose just 0.1%, with manufacturing unchanged and mining and utilities each up 0.4%. Capacity utilization held at 76.1%, 3.3 percentage points below its long-run average.

Housing starts looked much stronger, jumping 19.0% to an annualized 1.427 million, but multifamily construction drove the increase. Single-family starts slipped 0.2% to 895,000. Permits fell 3.0% to 1.367 million, including a 2.4% decline in single-family permits to 871,000. Completions rose 3.3%, with single-family completions up 6.6%. More construction and completed supply therefore did not establish a comparable acceleration in households' underlying demand for homes.

Import prices, meanwhile, kept the inflation pipeline in view. They rose 0.3% in June after a revised 1.7% May gain and were up 7.1% over the year, the largest annual increase since August 2022. Fuel imports fell 0.4% after May's 12.6% jump, but nonfuel prices increased 0.4% on the month and 4.2% on the year. Export prices declined 0.6% after a revised 1.2% increase. The improvement was thus less comprehensive than the earlier consumer- and producer-price reports might have suggested.

Preliminary consumer sentiment reached a five-month high as cheaper gasoline improved morale. One-year inflation expectations fell to 4.2% from 4.6%. By Friday's close, however, the fuel backdrop had changed again: the latest oil surge threatened to erode an improvement based on earlier gasoline relief.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack emphasized that risk. She ranked inflation above labor-market weakness, described employment as near her estimate of maximum employment and cited business concerns involving energy, supply chains, insurance and AI demand. Her remarks added to the hawkish case made by Lorie Logan the previous day, even as the week's inflation readings reduced the urgency of action at the next meeting. The question was increasingly when persistent pressure might force a response, rather than whether July's previously feared hike would occur.

The 5-year yield was unchanged at 4.28%. With shorter maturities resisting the long-end rally, 2s10s narrowed 4 basis points to 37 and 2s30s finished at 88. The weekly move remained modest despite the large swings around individual releases: 2-, 5- and 10-year yields were lower by 3, 2 and 1 basis points, respectively, while the 30-year was unchanged. All four remained 12–13 basis points above their month-earlier levels.

Real yields fell across the curve beyond the front end. Five- and seven-year yields each declined 3 basis points to 2.01% and 2.15%; 20- and 30-year yields each fell 4 to 2.67% and 2.87%. At ten years, rising inflation compensation absorbed half of the 4-basis-point real-yield decline, leaving the nominal yield down only 2. Short bills eased while longer bills stayed firmer, with the 52-week yield reaching 4.00%. There was little indication of immediate cash pressure, but the policy-sensitive part of the curve continued to allow for higher rates later on.

## Refinancings get done, at a price

Cotality resolved the placement question that had remained open at Thursday's close. The property-data company raised $5.25 billion, moving part of the package from bonds into loans after weak initial demand. Its $2.8 billion term loan priced at 98 with a 425-basis-point spread. A $1.65 billion first-lien bond priced at par to yield 9%, while an $800 million second-lien bond priced at 95 to yield about 13.3%, the highest yield on a US junk bond issued this year.

Investors also secured stronger protection against out-of-court restructuring maneuvers. The transaction refinances debt from a $6 billion acquisition five years earlier, but leaves a company rated six notches below investment grade, with debt near eight times earnings and only about $55 million of March-end cash, facing greater debt-service costs. Very modest expected free cash flow and reliance on a revolver remained relevant after the immediate financing hurdle was cleared.

For investment-grade investors, the new detail was the scale and breadth of hyperscaler bond underperformance. Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Oracle had issued more than $300 billion since the start of 2025, including almost $80 billion in sterling, euros, yen and other non-dollar currencies. About 79% of those bonds traded at wider spreads than on their first day. On average, prices were 3.3 points below issue and total returns were −1.4%, among the weakest in the markets where they had been sold.

Supply had accumulated faster than many portfolios expected. The issuers expanded into foreign markets as their funding needs exceeded what the dollar market alone could readily absorb. Amazon's latest $25 billion transaction had unusually low oversubscription for a jumbo AI deal. Insurers still had capacity, but benchmark-constrained buyers were already accumulating exposure through rising index weights. A continuing capital program meant that weaker sentiment about AI returns could coincide with more bonds to place, rather than an automatic reduction in borrowing.

SoftBank was pursuing another funding channel, planning about ¥60 billion of institutional notes after ¥678 billion of domestic retail subordinated bonds and earlier dollar and euro issuance. Its AI commitments included almost $65 billion to OpenAI. A contemplated loan secured against that stake had been reduced to about $6 billion from an initial $10 billion. The BB+ borrower still had access to retail, institutional, overseas and secured funding, but the range of channels also reflected the size of the commitments being financed.

Foundever's agreement addressed debt that could no longer remain on its original terms. Participating creditors were set to exchange existing claims into a new term loan at 57.5 cents on the dollar, receive roughly 35% of the restructured equity and share a $250 million cash paydown. The Mulliez family would provide $225 million of new equity and the company the balance. Debt was expected to fall about $900 million, with steering-committee lenders receiving an additional 10 cents of recovery. The outcome differed materially according to a creditor's position in the negotiation.

Aston Martin, meanwhile, was discussing financing secured on assets transferred beyond existing creditors' reach through a drop-down. Its sterling 2029 bonds fell almost 10 pence to 61 after bondholders had already organized over subordination concerns. Howden was considering the opposite route to balance-sheet repair: a large equity raise and eventual listing at a targeted £50 billion valuation, using proceeds to reduce senior debt at 5.1 times earnings following about 250 acquisitions in five years.

The roughly $1.3 trillion CLO market faced a separate squeeze on the equity return left after debt funding costs. Weak loan performance, software losses and a shortage of merger-related loan supply had compressed the available spread between asset income and financing expense. That did not mean senior funding had stopped, but it could make incremental loan demand more price-sensitive and encourage managers to consider infrastructure or equipment assets with different cash flows.

The issuance pipeline remained active. Deutsche Bank was preparing roughly $3 billion of debt for Baker Tilly to replace private-credit loans associated with the Moss Adams merger. San Antonio outlined a $944 million municipal sale for a 20-year airport expansion, including a new terminal costing about $1.7 billion.

Public infrastructure also supplied a contractual warning. Canada had financed the entire C$6.4 billion construction cost of the Gordie Howe bridge, but a new arrangement gave the US 50% of net operating revenue for the first 15 years without explicitly deducting Canada's interest or principal payments. The earlier framework allowed Canada to retain tolls until its debt was repaid. The change made the order of payments, traffic and toll policy more important to assessing Canada's recovery of its financing costs.

Broad credit funds reflected far less stress than some individual borrowers. LQD rose 0.06% to 107.56, while HYG fell 0.19% to 79.65 and JNK 0.10% to 95.98. Those modest moves sat alongside completed refinancings, substantial creditor concessions and growing supply burdens rather than a uniform withdrawal of market access.

## Europe gets inflation relief; Japan's normalization remains in view

Euro-area annual HICP slowed to 2.8% in June from 3.2% in May, matching the preliminary reading, while prices fell 0.1% on the month. Services contributed 1.51 percentage points to annual inflation, energy 0.77, food, alcohol and tobacco 0.29, and non-energy industrial goods 0.18. Inflation declined in 22 EU countries. The breadth of the slowdown strengthened the case for waiting, although inflation remained above its year-earlier level.

Economists expected the ECB to hold in July, with most anticipating a quarter-point September increase to a 2.5% deposit rate once new forecasts were available. Officials had seen little evidence of wages embedding the energy shock, though Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel remained vigilant. Renewed disruption to fuel supply could still change the outlook faster than the historical June data.

Reporting ahead of the BOJ meeting suggested officials would keep the policy rate at 1% after June's increase and consider raising the 0.5% growth forecast for the fiscal year ending next March. AI-related exports had supported profits and incomes despite expensive energy imports, while faster corporate cost pass-through and above-target inflation kept another hike in prospect. Swaps assigned about a 69% probability of action by October.

Japan's 3-month bill auction cleared at a 0.9618% weighted-average yield and 0.9695% at the lowest accepted price. Competitive bids of ¥11.5723 trillion compared with ¥2.89786 trillion accepted, alongside ¥902.10 billion of noncompetitive awards. The security issues July 21 and matures October 19. Demand for cash instruments was functioning, even as the eventual policy path and longer JGB supply remained separate questions.

Officials also continued to emphasize domestic investment by the ¥293.6 trillion GPIF. Its strategic allocations remained 25% each to Japanese bonds, Japanese equities, foreign bonds and foreign equities; no change had been made. The remarks were relevant to the debate over domestic demand and the weak yen, but did not establish a new purchase flow. Europe's disinflation and Japan's stronger growth outlook therefore continued to pull overseas duration demand in different directions.

## Oil exposure and funding choices separate emerging markets

EMB fell 0.06% to 95.53, leaving losses of 0.48% over the week and 1.18% over the month. With the dollar nearly unchanged at the NY close, oil was the more important source of divergence: potential revenue support for exporters came alongside higher import, subsidy and inflation costs elsewhere.

India was particularly exposed. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra described inflation as elevated after it exceeded the central bank's target for the first time in almost a year and a half. India imports nearly 90% of its oil, with almost half of those flows historically passing through Hormuz. The RBI held at 5.25%, the rupee was near 96.32 per dollar and the 10-year government yield around 6.75%. Renewed attacks and a weak monsoon could make it harder to look through higher imported costs.

Brazil was considering an inaugural onshore Chinese panda bond of about CNY10 billion, or $1.48 billion, as soon as this year. Officials hoped a sovereign benchmark would open renminbi funding to companies with substantial Chinese operations. Foreign-exchange-linked debt represented only 4% of Brazil's total, and the country had already raised €5 billion in its largest global transaction and first euro offering in more than a decade. The proposed panda deal would add a funding market, not replace the existing dollar base.

Argentina's oil-producing Neuquén province was seeking its first international issue since 2017. It had authorization for up to $500 million and targeted a five- to seven-year bullet bond at 7%–8%. Stronger shale output supported the revenue case, while narrower Argentine spreads had allowed several provinces to issue even as the national government stayed out. A single repayment date and commodity dependence remained important features of that access.

Chile's government argued that corporate tax cuts and faster investment permits could lift 2027 growth to 3.7%, versus 2.7% without the package, and leave gross debt at 44.2% of GDP in 2029 rather than 45.3%. The improvement depended on growth offsetting lost revenue. Analysts warned that exceeding the government's 45% prudential debt threshold could threaten the rating, making the assumed response of investment and activity central to the fiscal case.

## Technology weakens while crude surges

The S&P 500 fell 1.01%, the Nasdaq 100 1.49% and the semiconductor index 1.63%. Semiconductors finished the week down 9.97% and more than 12% below a month earlier; VIX rose 12.19% to 18.77. Technology remained the focus of the retreat, rather than losses spreading indiscriminately through credit.

A low-cost model from China's Moonshot added to questions about competition and the return on infrastructure spending. Current earnings and demand had not broken, but valuations were becoming less forgiving of long payback periods. The equity weakness gave duration support while the continuing need to fund construction kept pressure on hyperscaler bonds.

WTI surged 4.48% to $82.49 and Brent 4.59% to $88.10 as US-Iran attacks continued, bringing weekly gains to 15.52% and 15.91%. The rise helps explain why inflation compensation increased even while long Treasuries rallied, and why policy-sensitive maturities did not share the bid. It also threatened the earlier gasoline relief reflected in consumer expectations.

The dollar index was almost flat at 100.75 and slightly lower over the week. Gold futures gained 0.68% to $4,012.70 but still lost 2.23% for the week. Haven demand was uneven: lower real yields helped bullion recover some ground, but the prospect of energy keeping policy rates high remained a competing consideration.

In early Monday Asian trading, Brent rose as much as 3.8% to above $91 as strikes expanded beyond military targets, and the dollar strengthened against most peers. A Japanese holiday kept cash Treasury trading closed during Asian hours. The later escalation left investors waiting for the rates response to a further energy shock, distinct from Friday's completed close.

## Inflation protection and housing lead the next US tests

The $21 billion new 10-year TIPS auction on July 23 at 13:00 ET will test demand for real duration and inflation protection after oil's surge. June new-home sales follow July 24 at 10:00. Auction absorption and housing demand will help show whether Friday's lower real yields can persist alongside higher energy-driven inflation compensation before the July 28–29 Fed meeting.

The ECB decision on July 23 and UK retail sales on July 24 at 02:00 ET will add a European perspective. June disinflation and limited wage spillovers favor patience; policy language and household spending will show how much room remains if the energy shock continues.

Japan's national CPI on July 24 precedes the BOJ decision. Broad, elevated inflation alongside an improved growth outlook would sustain expectations of further normalization; evidence of softer prices or pressure on household demand would support waiting. The implications extend beyond the next rate move to JGB demand, the yen and the relative attraction of overseas bonds to Japanese investors.
